result.topic_en: A derivation showing that, among all linear combinations of the observation equations that yield the unknown x, the one whose coefficients have the minimum sum of squares is the one given by the method of least squares (Gauss–Markov type argument).
result.transcription:
Gaussisches[?] Meth. d. kl. Qu. {+Bö+}
Es seyn vorgegeben die linearen Gleichungen der unbek. Grössen $x, y, z$ u.s.w.
$V=0,\ V'=0,\ V''=0$ etc.
wo $V, V', V''$ u.s.w. folgende Functionen vorstellen
$V = ax + by + cz + \text{etc.} + m$
$V' = a'x + b'y + c'z + \text{etc.} + m'$
$V'' = a''x + b''y + c''z + \text{etc.} + m''$
etc.
Es sei [-ax-] zur Bestimmung von $x$, [-die vortheilhafteste-] {+eine+} Combination der Gleichungen $V=0, V'=0, V''=0$ etc. diese
$pV + p'V' + p''V'' + \text{etc.} = 0$
welche geben möge
[-a-] $x - k = 0$
{+man sucht+} [-die unter allen Systemen-] von Coefficienten [-seyn-] die ein Resultat dieser Form geben haben $p, p', p''$ etc. die Eigenschaft dass $pp + p'p' + p''p''$ u.s.w. ein Minimum werde.
Auflösung. Es sei $\Sigma aV = \xi,\ \Sigma bV = \eta,\ \Sigma cV = \zeta$ etc. und durch Elimination ergebe sich
$A\xi + B\eta + C\zeta + \text{etc.} = x - \alpha$
wo demnach $\alpha$ der nach der sogen. Methode der kleinsten Quadrate bestimmte Werth von $x$ ist.
Man hat also indefinite, wenn man
$aA + bB + cC + \text{etc.} = \varpi$
$a'A + b'B + c'C + \text{etc.} = \varpi'$
$a''A + b''B + c''C + \text{etc.} = \varpi''$
etc.
setzt
$x - \alpha = \varpi V + \varpi' V' + \varpi'' V'' + \text{etc.}$
Es wird daher indefinite seyn
$(p-\varpi)V + (p'-\varpi')V' + (p''-\varpi'')V'' + \text{etc.} = \alpha - k$
folglich
$(p-\varpi)a + (p'-\varpi')a' + (p''-\varpi'')a'' + \text{etc.} = 0$
$(p-\varpi)b + (p'-\varpi')b' + (p''-\varpi'')b'' + \text{etc.} = 0$
$(p-\varpi)c + (p'-\varpi')c' + (p''-\varpi'')c'' + \text{etc.} = 0$
u.s.w. also auch wenn man diese Gl. mit $A, B, C$ u.s.w. [-addirt-] {+multiplicirt,+} und addirt
$(p-\varpi)\varpi + (p'-\varpi')\varpi' + (p''-\varpi'')\varpi'' + \text{etc.} = 0$ also
$pp + p'p' + p''p'' + \text{etc.} = \varpi\varpi + \varpi'\varpi' + \varpi''\varpi'' + \text{etc.} + (p-\varpi)^2 + (p'-\varpi')^2 + (p''-\varpi'')^2 + \text{etc.}$
$= A + (p-\varpi)^2 + (p'-\varpi')^2 + (p''-\varpi'')^2 + \text{etc.}$
Diese Grösse wird daher offenbar am kleinsten wenn $p=\varpi,\ p'=\varpi',\ p''=\varpi''$ u.s.w.

methods.what: Linear system of observation equations with unknowns x, y, z
Normal equations via sums ξ=ΣaV etc. and their elimination giving the least-squares estimate α of x
Least-squares coefficients ϖ expressed through the elimination coefficients A, B, C
x − α as linear combination of the V's with least-squares weights
Orthogonality condition of the difference (p−ϖ) with ϖ
Pythagorean decomposition of sum of squares of coefficients; Σϖϖ = A
Minimum-variance (Gauss–Markov) optimality of least squares: minimum attained at p=ϖ
